To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ESCRT-III VPS-20 adopts a conformation that is distinct from other ESCRT-3 subunits, and that VPS-20 is not auto-inhibited in solution, but is activated upon interaction with ESCRT-II.
ESCRT-II and ESCRT-III directly interact in solution and that the ESCRT-II/VPS-20 complex adopts an open conformation.
the ESCRT-3 subunit VPS-20 adopts an open conformation and that it directly interacts with the ESCRT-II subunit VPS25 in vitro and in vitro, irrespective of the membrane context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of ESCRT-mediated membrane remodeling.
the structural characterization of VPS-20 and its interaction with ESCRT-II.
understanding the mechanisms that underlie ESCRT-mediated membrane remodelling and the regulation of this process in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Vps20 adopts a conformational state that differs from that of Vps24 and that the conformational state of ESCRT- III proteins is likely to be determined by their function.
VPS-20 adopts an open conformation and that the ESCRT-2-VPS-20 complex is a pre-assembly complex.
VPS-20 is a unique member of the ESCRT-iii complex and it is the only ESCRT-iii subunit that is not regulated by auto-inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ESCRT-II and ESCRT-III proteins can form complexes in solution, and that the conformation of ESCRT-3 subunits can be different from one another.
the VPS-20 isoform of ESCRT-iii has an open extended confor-mation in the absence of ESCRT-ii, and that the ESCRT-ii-VPS-20 complex is not auto-inhibited.
ESCRT-II and ESCRT-III interact directly in the absence of membranes and that ESCRT-III proteins exhibit different conformations depending on their specific roles during membrane reorganization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESCRT-3/VPS-20 complex adopts a different conformation than the ESCRT-1/VPS-24 complex, and that the ESCRT-II/VPS-20 interaction is not mediated by ESCRT-II membrane binding.
the ESCRT-2/VPS20 complex is active in solution and that VPS20 is not auto-inhibited by its C-terminal domain, in contrast with other ESCRT-3 subunits.
